## 1. Purpose

This module defines the nested cross-validation design used by every
genomic-prediction method fitted to the real *Coffea arabica* population. The
partitions are created before model fitting and are reused unchanged by
GBLUP-ADE and all ANN variants.

The validation design has four fixed features:

- **Repeated outer cross-validation:** 5 repetitions of 5 outer folds provide
  25 held-out evaluations.
- **Nested inner cross-validation:** each outer analysis set is divided into 4
  inner folds for ANN model selection.
- **Common partitions:** the same outer and inner assignments are reused for
  `Cer`, `BM`, `LP`, GBLUP-ADE, and all ANN configurations.
- **Information separation:** BLUP values, genomic marker values, and model
  identity do not participate in fold generation.

Throughout this module, **analysis set** denotes individuals available for model
development at the current validation level, whereas **assessment set** denotes
individuals held out for evaluation at that level.

## 2. Package and fixed validation settings

`knitr` is used to present validation settings and partition summaries as
reader-facing tables.

```{r packages, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(knitr)
```

The partitioning procedure is controlled by four fixed values.

```{r validation-parameters}
SEED_GLOBAL <- 20261105L
N_OUTER_REPEATS <- 5L
N_OUTER_FOLDS <- 5L
N_INNER_FOLDS <- 4L

validation_parameters <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c(
    "Global seed",
    "Outer repetitions",
    "Outer folds per repetition",
    "Inner folds per outer split"
  ),
  Value = c(
    SEED_GLOBAL,
    N_OUTER_REPEATS,
    N_OUTER_FOLDS,
    N_INNER_FOLDS
  ),
  Role = c(
    "reproducible partition generation",
    "repeat held-out evaluation",
    "define outer assessment sets",
    "compare ANN candidates inside each outer analysis set"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

validation_parameters |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Fixed nested cross-validation settings",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

## 3. Population entering validation

The validation module reads only the common object prepared in the preceding
data-preparation stage. The 195 aligned individuals and the common genomic
matrix are therefore fixed before partition generation.

```{r validation-input}
common <- readRDS(
  "output/real/audit/preprocessed_real_common.rds"
)

ids <- rownames(
  common$genotype
)

input_summary <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Individuals",
    "Prediction traits",
    "Markers after common QC"
  ),
  Value = c(
    length(ids),
    paste(common$traits, collapse = ", "),
    ncol(common$genotype)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Real-data population entering validation",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )

stopifnot(
  length(ids) == 195L,
  length(unique(ids)) == 195L,
  nrow(common$phenotype) == 195L,
  identical(
    ids,
    common$phenotype$Phenotype_ID
  ),
  identical(
    common$traits,
    c("Cer", "BM", "LP")
  ),
  ncol(common$genotype) == 20887L
)
```

Only the individual identifiers and deterministic seeds are used to create the
folds. Phenotypic targets and genomic marker values remain outside partition
generation.

## 4. Repeated outer cross-validation

In each repetition, the 195 individuals are randomly shuffled and divided into
five folds of equal size. Because 195 is exactly divisible by five, every outer
assessment fold contains 39 individuals and the remaining 156 individuals form
the corresponding outer analysis set.

### 4.1 Outer fold assignments

```{r outer-folds}
outer_assignment_list <- vector(
  "list",
  N_OUTER_REPEATS
)

outer_splits <- list()

for (rep_id in seq_len(N_OUTER_REPEATS)) {

  set.seed(
    SEED_GLOBAL + rep_id
  )

  shuffled_ids <- sample(
    ids,
    size = length(ids),
    replace = FALSE
  )

  assigned_folds <- rep(
    seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS),
    each = length(ids) / N_OUTER_FOLDS
  )

  assignment <- data.frame(
    Repetition = rep_id,
    ID = shuffled_ids,
    OuterFold = assigned_folds,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  assignment <- assignment[
    order(assignment$ID),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  rownames(
    assignment
  ) <- NULL

  assignment$SplitID <- sprintf(
    "R%02d_F%02d",
    assignment$Repetition,
    assignment$OuterFold
  )

  outer_assignment_list[[rep_id]] <- assignment

  for (outer_fold in seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {

    split_id <- sprintf(
      "R%02d_F%02d",
      rep_id,
      outer_fold
    )

    assessment_ids <- assignment$ID[
      assignment$OuterFold == outer_fold
    ]

    analysis_ids <- ids[
      !ids %in% assessment_ids
    ]

    outer_splits[[split_id]] <- list(
      split_id = split_id,
      repetition = rep_id,
      outer_fold = outer_fold,
      analysis_ids = analysis_ids,
      assessment_ids = assessment_ids
    )
  }
}

outer_assignments <- do.call(
  rbind,
  outer_assignment_list
)

rownames(
  outer_assignments
) <- NULL
```

### 4.2 Outer split checks

```{r outer-checks}
outer_split_ids <- names(
  outer_splits
)

outer_sizes_list <- vector(
  "list",
  length(outer_split_ids)
)

for (i in seq_along(outer_split_ids)) {

  split_id <- outer_split_ids[i]
  current_split <- outer_splits[[split_id]]

  outer_sizes_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
    SplitID = split_id,
    Analysis_N = length(
      current_split$analysis_ids
    ),
    Assessment_N = length(
      current_split$assessment_ids
    ),
    Overlap_N = length(
      intersect(
        current_split$analysis_ids,
        current_split$assessment_ids
      )
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

outer_sizes <- do.call(
  rbind,
  outer_sizes_list
)

rownames(
  outer_sizes
) <- NULL

outer_coverage <- TRUE

for (rep_id in seq_len(N_OUTER_REPEATS)) {

  assessed <- character(0)

  for (outer_fold in seq_len(N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {

    split_id <- sprintf(
      "R%02d_F%02d",
      rep_id,
      outer_fold
    )

    assessed <- c(
      assessed,
      outer_splits[[split_id]]$assessment_ids
    )
  }

  if (
    length(assessed) != 195L ||
    !identical(
      sort(assessed),
      sort(ids)
    ) ||
    any(table(assessed) != 1L)
  ) {
    outer_coverage <- FALSE
  }
}

outer_contract <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "25 outer splits",
    "156 analysis individuals per split",
    "39 assessment individuals per split",
    "No analysis-assessment overlap",
    "Every individual assessed exactly once per repetition"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    length(outer_splits) == 25L,
    all(outer_sizes$Analysis_N == 156L),
    all(outer_sizes$Assessment_N == 39L),
    all(outer_sizes$Overlap_N == 0L),
    outer_coverage
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

outer_contract |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Outer validation design checks",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )

stopifnot(
  all(outer_contract$Passed)
)
```

Across the complete outer design, every individual is assessed once in each
repetition and five times in total.

## 5. Nested inner cross-validation

Each outer analysis set contains 156 individuals. Within each outer split,
these individuals are randomly shuffled and divided into four equal inner folds.

Each inner assessment set therefore contains 39 individuals, while the
remaining 117 individuals form the corresponding inner analysis set. The outer
assessment individuals do not participate in inner partition generation.

### 5.1 Inner fold assignments

```{r inner-folds}
inner_assignments_list <- vector(
  "list",
  length(outer_splits)
)

names(
  inner_assignments_list
) <- names(
  outer_splits
)

inner_splits <- vector(
  "list",
  length(outer_splits)
)

names(
  inner_splits
) <- names(
  outer_splits
)

for (split_id in names(outer_splits)) {

  outer_split <- outer_splits[[split_id]]

  rep_id <- outer_split$repetition
  outer_fold <- outer_split$outer_fold

  outer_analysis_ids <- outer_split$analysis_ids

  set.seed(
    SEED_GLOBAL +
      100000L +
      rep_id * 100L +
      outer_fold
  )

  shuffled_inner_ids <- sample(
    outer_analysis_ids,
    size = length(outer_analysis_ids),
    replace = FALSE
  )

  assigned_inner_folds <- rep(
    seq_len(N_INNER_FOLDS),
    each = length(outer_analysis_ids) / N_INNER_FOLDS
  )

  inner_assignment <- data.frame(
    SplitID = split_id,
    Repetition = rep_id,
    OuterFold = outer_fold,
    ID = shuffled_inner_ids,
    InnerFold = assigned_inner_folds,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  inner_assignment <- inner_assignment[
    order(inner_assignment$ID),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  rownames(
    inner_assignment
  ) <- NULL

  inner_assignments_list[[split_id]] <- inner_assignment

  current_inner_splits <- vector(
    "list",
    N_INNER_FOLDS
  )

  names(
    current_inner_splits
  ) <- paste0(
    "I",
    seq_len(N_INNER_FOLDS)
  )

  for (inner_fold in seq_len(N_INNER_FOLDS)) {

    assessment_ids <- inner_assignment$ID[
      inner_assignment$InnerFold == inner_fold
    ]

    analysis_ids <- outer_analysis_ids[
      !outer_analysis_ids %in% assessment_ids
    ]

    current_inner_splits[[paste0("I", inner_fold)]] <- list(
      split_id = split_id,
      inner_fold = inner_fold,
      analysis_ids = analysis_ids,
      assessment_ids = assessment_ids
    )
  }

  inner_splits[[split_id]] <- current_inner_splits
}

inner_assignments <- do.call(
  rbind,
  inner_assignments_list
)

rownames(
  inner_assignments
) <- NULL
```

### 5.2 Inner split checks

```{r inner-checks}
inner_sizes_list <- vector(
  "list",
  length(outer_splits) * N_INNER_FOLDS
)

inner_row <- 1L
outer_leakage <- FALSE
inner_coverage <- TRUE

for (split_id in names(inner_splits)) {

  outer_analysis <- outer_splits[[split_id]]$analysis_ids
  outer_assessment <- outer_splits[[split_id]]$assessment_ids
  inner_assessed <- character(0)

  for (inner_name in names(inner_splits[[split_id]])) {

    current_inner <- inner_splits[[split_id]][[inner_name]]

    inner_sizes_list[[inner_row]] <- data.frame(
      SplitID = split_id,
      InnerFold = current_inner$inner_fold,
      Analysis_N = length(
        current_inner$analysis_ids
      ),
      Assessment_N = length(
        current_inner$assessment_ids
      ),
      Overlap_N = length(
        intersect(
          current_inner$analysis_ids,
          current_inner$assessment_ids
        )
      ),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    inner_assessed <- c(
      inner_assessed,
      current_inner$assessment_ids
    )

    inner_ids <- c(
      current_inner$analysis_ids,
      current_inner$assessment_ids
    )

    if (
      length(
        intersect(
          outer_assessment,
          inner_ids
        )
      ) > 0L
    ) {
      outer_leakage <- TRUE
    }

    inner_row <- inner_row + 1L
  }

  if (
    length(inner_assessed) != 156L ||
    !identical(
      sort(inner_assessed),
      sort(outer_analysis)
    ) ||
    any(table(inner_assessed) != 1L)
  ) {
    inner_coverage <- FALSE
  }
}

inner_sizes <- do.call(
  rbind,
  inner_sizes_list
)

rownames(
  inner_sizes
) <- NULL

inner_contract <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "100 inner splits",
    "117 inner-analysis individuals per split",
    "39 inner-assessment individuals per split",
    "No inner analysis-assessment overlap",
    "Every outer-analysis individual assessed once across the four inner folds",
    "No outer-assessment individual enters inner validation"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    nrow(inner_sizes) == 100L,
    all(inner_sizes$Analysis_N == 117L),
    all(inner_sizes$Assessment_N == 39L),
    all(inner_sizes$Overlap_N == 0L),
    inner_coverage,
    !outer_leakage
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

inner_contract |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Nested inner-validation design checks",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )

stopifnot(
  all(inner_contract$Passed)
)
```

The inner assessment sets are used only for model selection within the
corresponding outer analysis sample. The outer assessment set remains untouched
until final prediction for that split.

## 6. Information used to create partitions

The fold-generation variables are separated explicitly from the information
used later for genomic prediction.

```{r partition-information}
partition_information <- data.frame(
  Information = c(
    "Individual ID",
    "Deterministic seed",
    "Cer BLUP",
    "BM BLUP",
    "LP BLUP",
    "Genomic marker values",
    "Prediction model"
  ),
  Partition_role = c(
    "Used",
    "Used",
    "Not used",
    "Not used",
    "Not used",
    "Not used",
    "Not used"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

partition_information |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Information used and excluded during partition generation",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

The same stored partitions are therefore valid for all three prediction traits
and all prediction methods.

## 7. Validation design summary

```{r validation-summary}
design_summary <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Individuals",
    "Outer repetitions",
    "Outer folds per repetition",
    "Total outer splits",
    "Outer analysis N",
    "Outer assessment N",
    "Inner folds per outer split",
    "Total inner splits",
    "Inner analysis N",
    "Inner assessment N"
  ),
  Value = c(
    length(ids),
    N_OUTER_REPEATS,
    N_OUTER_FOLDS,
    length(outer_splits),
    unique(outer_sizes$Analysis_N),
    unique(outer_sizes$Assessment_N),
    N_INNER_FOLDS,
    nrow(inner_sizes),
    unique(inner_sizes$Analysis_N),
    unique(inner_sizes$Assessment_N)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

design_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Common real-data validation design",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered" style="width:100%;"'
  )
```

## 8. Common validation object

The stored validation object contains the assignment tables and explicit ID
vectors required by the subsequent model-fitting modules.

```{r build-validation-object}
cv_design <- list(
  dataset = "real",
  seed_global = SEED_GLOBAL,
  n_outer_repeats = N_OUTER_REPEATS,
  n_outer_folds = N_OUTER_FOLDS,
  n_inner_folds = N_INNER_FOLDS,
  ids = ids,
  outer_assignments = outer_assignments,
  outer_splits = outer_splits,
  inner_assignments = inner_assignments,
  inner_splits = inner_splits,
  checks = list(
    outer_contract = outer_contract,
    inner_contract = inner_contract,
    outer_coverage = outer_coverage,
    inner_coverage = inner_coverage,
    outer_leakage = outer_leakage
  )
)
```

```{r save-validation-outputs, include=FALSE}
saveRDS(
  cv_design,
  "output/real/validation/real_cv_design.rds",
  compress = "gzip"
)

write.csv(
  outer_assignments,
  "output/real/validation/real_outer_assignments.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  inner_assignments,
  "output/real/validation/real_inner_assignments.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  design_summary,
  "output/real/validation/real_validation_summary.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## 9. Validation input for genomic prediction

The primary model comparison uses the same 25 outer assessment sets for
GBLUP-ADE and every ANN configuration. ANN model selection is restricted to the
100 inner splits nested within the corresponding outer analysis sets.

No phenotypic or genomic values are used to create the validation partitions.
